newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Siu-Fung says in cashflow problems.
newsitem.headline: HK's Siu-Fung says in cashflow problems.

text.p: Siu-fung Ceramics Holdings Ltd said on Friday it and its subsidiaries were in serious cashflow problems mainly due to deterioration in the financial condition of operations of its NHD subsidiaries in Germany.
"The group is currently experiencing serious cashflow problems," chairman Siegfried Lee of the ceramics and machinery maker said in the statement.

The problems in Germany led to the appointment of a court- appointed sequester in relation to six companies in NHD group, which may or may not result in the commencement of bankruptcy proceedings for some or all of those companies, Lee said.
The sequester was expected to finalise his report within four to 10 weeks after his appointment in late October.
Lee added a number of ceramics manufacturing operations in China were still requiring additional capital investment and were currently not generating significant income for the group.
The statement also said Siu-Fung's manufacturing operations in China were at an early stage of construction and operation.
Of the 31 plants in China, 15 are in operation, three have been temporarily closed, ten are at start-up mode and three are under construction, it said.
Siu-Fung said it was in discussions with the banks to identify its immediate funding requirements and alternatives for restructuring its exisiting short-term and long-term indebtness.
The board was also exploring other sources of funding other than banks, and a report from its auditors about its financial requirements was expected by the end of the month, it said.
The company said it was also considering possible asset disposals but that no agreements had yet been reached.
Trading of Siu-Fung shares, which has been suspended since October 28, will remain suspended pending further notice, it said.
